note: Register-routing briefs for the static-design plugin (the B-iii eval from the 19 Aug 2026 brief). Each brief states what assets were supplied; the session must name the picture structure in its five-line plan before designing. The prompts carry no design direction — choosing the structure is what 04-graphics-imagery's routing table is for. Expected values: A, B, C, TYPE (type-led), DATA (data-led). Where two are acceptable, list both.

evals.name: one-photo-evidence
evals.prompt: A 4:5 tile: 75% of Australians want the algorithm regulated (Essential Report, July 2026, all participants, n=1,060). Supplied: one full-frame photograph of a woman lit by her phone screen, dark studio, no cutout.
evals.wrong_and_why: C would crop through a subject that cannot be cut; type-led throws the evidence away.

evals.name: one-cutout-plus-glyphs
evals.prompt: A 4:5 tile: 75% of Australians want the algorithm regulated (Essential Report, July 2026, all participants, n=1,060). Supplied: one silhouette-cut, halftoned PNG of the Prime Minister at a lectern, and a set of flat single-colour glyphs — a bell, a speech bubble, a play triangle.
evals.wrong_and_why: A blows the cutout up full-bleed with no scene and dims it under the type; B buries the one subject under invented density.

evals.name: ten-cutouts
evals.prompt: A 4:5 cover for a report on trust in institutions. Supplied: eleven silhouette-cut photographic elements in one register — a gavel, a ballot box, a microphone, three portraits, a building, a hand, a phone, a newspaper, a flag — all keyed with alpha.
evals.wrong_and_why: A or C leaves nine assets unused or stacks eleven satellites where six was the ceiling — the sticker sheet.

evals.name: four-photos-pinboard
evals.prompt: A 4:5 tile: 75% of Australians want the algorithm regulated (Essential Report, July 2026, all participants, n=1,060). Supplied: four rectangular photographs — a phone in a hand, a server room, a woman at a laptop, a street at night. None is cut out.
evals.wrong_and_why: Four photographs arranged on a field is the pinboard (06-V). Pick the one strong photograph and build A; the linter fails a four-photo frame.

evals.name: no-assets-one-number
evals.prompt: A 4:5 tile: 75% of Australians want the algorithm regulated (Essential Report, July 2026, all participants, n=1,060). Nothing supplied.
evals.wrong_and_why: Any picture structure means a stock photograph standing in for evidence or a cutout nobody cut. One number is a stat tile, not a chart.

evals.name: cutout-no-glyphs
evals.prompt: A 4:5 tile: 75% of Australians want the algorithm regulated (Essential Report, July 2026, all participants, n=1,060). Supplied: one silhouette-cut PNG of a person holding a phone. No glyphs, no second asset, no window object named.
evals.wrong_and_why: A cutout is not a full-frame photograph, so A is out — blown up it is a sticker with nothing behind it. C is legal only if the session draws a glyph vocabulary the story owns (three to six flat glyphs); otherwise type- or data-led with the cutout as the single foreign-register element (04's exception). Live run 19 Aug 2026: the plugin chose data-led with the halftoned silhouette breaking the right edge — correct, and the original expectation (C/A) was the eval's error, since fixed with the routing table.

evals.name: two-cutouts-subject-and-mass
evals.prompt: A 4:5 tile: 75% of Australians want the algorithm regulated (Essential Report, July 2026, all participants, n=1,060). Supplied: one halftoned cutout of the Prime Minister and one duotoned cutout of Parliament House, both keyed, same duotone map; plus a bell and a speech-bubble glyph.
evals.wrong_and_why: Two photographs is not B. C's ground-mass build seats the subject with the second mass (08); read as two subjects it is a two-cutout pinboard.
